gam-ba-be-001-q1.rationale: Blind re-answer (independent-blind-1, confidence 0.97): Block l1 lists the assumptions and opens with 'Every unit produced is sold within the same period, so output and sales are equal', which is option a verbatim in paraphrase. Options b, c and d each directly contradict a stated assumption (constant price, unchanged fixed costs, single product). No second option is arguable. Full ablation (independent-ablation-1): determinable without the pack (would have chosen "a", confidence 0.75) — Standard CVP/break-even assumptions are textbook: production equals sales in the period, constant unit price, constant unit variable cost, single product, fixed costs constant over the range. Options b, c and d each name something the linear model explicitly excludes, so a is forced without any source.

gam-ba-be-001-q2.rationale: Blind re-answer (independent-blind-1, confidence 0.98): From f1 and p3: c = 40 - 25 = 15, q_BE = 90,000 / 15 = 6,000 units. The distractors are the classic wrong denominators — 2,250 = F/p and 3,600 = F/v — so each wrong method lands on a listed option. Only c is defensible. Full ablation (independent-ablation-1): determinable without the pack (would have chosen "c", confidence 0.7) — Cross-question leakage supplies every input: q3's stem gives fixed costs of 90,000 euros, q5's options give price 40 and variable cost 25 (contribution 15), so 90,000/15 = 6,000. q3's option b ('It stays at 6,000 units') independently confirms the baseline.

gam-cs-oc-001-q1.rationale: Blind re-answer (independent-blind-1, confidence 0.98): Table 1 gives SPLIT at n = 256 as 240, which the formula 25*log2(256) + 40 = 25*8 + 40 confirms. Straight table read; the distractors are the other two SPLIT entries and SCAN's 256 value. Full ablation (independent-ablation-1): determinable without the pack (would have chosen "b", confidence 0.65) — Recovered by exact arithmetic across the item set rather than from Table 1: q5's distractor 252,960 equals 240 x 1054 exactly and its option 1,294 equals 240 + 1054, while q7's 61,440 equals 256 x 240. Two independent exact products pin SPLIT(256) = 240.

gam-cs-oc-001-q2.rationale: Blind re-answer (independent-blind-1, confidence 0.97): 25*log2(1024) + 40 = 25*10 + 40 = 290. It is also reachable without any logarithm knowledge from the table alone: each quadrupling of n adds 50 to SPLIT, so 240 at n = 256 becomes 290 at n = 1024. That redundancy is why I judged no outside knowledge needed. Full ablation (independent-ablation-1): above-chance without the pack (would have chosen "b", confidence 0.5) — Given SPLIT(256) = 240 recovered above and SPLIT growing only from 240 to the 265-315 band as n quadruples, SPLIT must be logarithmic of the form a*log2(n) + b; only a = 25, b = 40 gives integer-friendly values (240 at n=256, 290 at n=1024). Option d (1,064 = n + 40) is the linear lure. Reconstruction, not knowledge.

adjudicator.model: independent-ablation-1 (full ablation) + independent-blind-1 (blind re-answer)

gam-cs-oc-001-q3.rationale: Blind re-answer (independent-blind-1, confidence 0.97): At n = 16, SCAN 94 < PAIR 128 < SPLIT 140, so SCAN is lowest. At n = 256 (1054 vs SPLIT 240) and n = 4096 (16414 vs SPLIT 340) it is not. Only 'n = 16 only' survives; the comparison must be against both rivals, and PAIR being cheaper than SPLIT at n = 16 is exactly the trap. Full ablation (independent-ablation-1): above-chance without the pack (would have chosen "a", confidence 0.45) — Table 1 is missing, but the reconstructed profile (SCAN linear with a large constant, ~1054 at n=256; SPLIT logarithmic, 240 at n=256) puts SCAN ahead only at the smallest size, and an item asking where a routine wins is normally written around a real crossover rather than keyed to 'none'. Design inference plus reconstruction, not a read.

gam-cs-oc-001-q4.rationale: Blind re-answer (independent-blind-1, confidence 0.97): T_PAIR = n^2/2 from f1, so doubling n multiplies the count by 4 (8192^2/2 divided by 4096^2/2 = 4). 'Roughly' is generous here since the factor is exactly 4. No second reading. Full ablation (independent-ablation-1): determinable without the pack (would have chosen "c", confidence 0.6) — The routine name PAIR signals all-pairs comparison, i.e. quadratic cost, so doubling n roughly quadruples the count. Standard complexity knowledge; the three-routine linear/logarithmic/quadratic set-up is also the conventional shape of such a table.

gam-cs-oc-001-q5.rationale: Blind re-answer (independent-blind-1, confidence 0.97): Block p3 says sequential runs add: 240 + 1054 = 1294. Option d (252,960 = 240*1054) is the multiply-instead-of-add trap and option c (1314) a slip. Only b is defensible. Full ablation (independent-ablation-1): determinable without the pack (would have chosen "b", confidence 0.7) — The option set is self-solving: 252,960 = 240 x 1054 and 1,294 = 240 + 1054, so the two table values must be 240 and 1054 and the sum asked for is 1,294. Option a is one addend alone and d is the product trap. No table required.

gam-cs-oc-001-q6.rationale: Blind re-answer (independent-blind-1, confidence 0.95): Checked all four against Table 1: SCAN is fewest at n = 16 (94), SPLIT at n = 256 and n = 4096, so neither a nor d holds, and b fails because at n = 16 SPLIT's 140 exceeds PAIR's 128. gam-cs-oc-001-q7.rationale: Blind re-answer (independent-blind-1, confidence 0.95): Block p3's multiplication rule applies: SPLIT runs once per record examined, 256 * 240 = 61,440, and the stem tells us to ignore SCAN's own steps. Full ablation (independent-ablation-1): determinable without the pack (would have chosen "d", confidence 0.6) — A scan examines all 256 records, and with SPLIT(256) = 240 recovered from the option arithmetic the total is 256 x 240 = 61,440, which appears verbatim as option d. gam-eng-tr-001-q1.rationale: Blind re-answer (independent-blind-1, confidence 0.98): Figure 2 states the brick layer is 0.24 m thick with conductivity 0.60. The distractors are the insulation thickness (0.08), the insulation conductivity (0.05) and the brick conductivity (0.60) — a clean figure-read item that punishes reading the wrong column. Full ablation (independent-ablation-1): determinable without the pack (would have chosen "c", confidence 0.6) — Domain plausibility settles it: 0.24 m is the standard masonry wall thickness, 0.05 and 0.08 m are insulation-board thicknesses, and 0.60 m is implausible for the wall described. q3's option a also asserts brick is the thicker of the two layers, which excludes the two small values.

adjudicator.model: independent-ablation-1 (full ablation) + independent-blind-1 (blind re-answer)

gam-eng-tr-001-q2.rationale: Blind re-answer (independent-blind-1, confidence 0.97): R_brick = 0.24/0.60 = 0.4 and R_ins = 0.08/0.05 = 1.6, total 2.0; Q = A*dT/R_total = 18*20/2.0 = 180 W, using only f1 and Figure 2. I tried the obvious wrong routes (using one layer's resistance alone, or averaging the conductivities) and none of them produces 90, 144 or 900, so the distractors are unreachable by a coherent alternative reading and 180 stands alone. Full ablation (independent-ablation-1): above-chance without the pack (would have chosen "c", confidence 0.45) — Conductivities, area and temperature difference are all in the missing figure, so no direct computation. But physics bounds it against q4: adding a second identical insulation layer can at most double total resistance, so the new flow lies in [Q/2, Q). That kills 900 W (no q4 partner) and 90 W (nothing lower available), leaving 144 or 180; the pair (180, 100) yields the clean R_insulation = 4 x R_brick that q3's key requires, whereas (144, 100) would make brick dominant and contradict q3.

adjudicator.model: independent-ablation-1 (full ablation) + independent-blind-1 (blind re-answer)

gam-eng-tr-001-q3.rationale: Blind re-answer (independent-blind-1, confidence 0.96): R_ins = 1.6 against R_brick = 0.4, so insulation carries four fifths of the resistance, and p2's 'a layer of low conductivity contributes a large resistance even when it is thin' supplies the reason. Option a picks the right kind of reason but the wrong layer; both halves of b are correct, which is what makes it uniquely defensible. Full ablation (independent-ablation-1): determinable without the pack (would have chosen "b", confidence 0.8) — R = d/lambda, and insulation conductivity is roughly an order of magnitude below brick, so insulation dominates total resistance despite being thinner. Option d also misstates series behaviour (equal heat flow does not mean equal resistance). No figure needed.

adjudicator.model: independent-ablation-1 (full ablation) + independent-blind-1 (blind re-answer)

gam-eng-tr-001-q4.rationale: Blind re-answer (independent-blind-1, confidence 0.96): New R_ins = 0.16/0.05 = 3.2, total 3.6, Q = 360/3.6 = 100 W. Option a (90 W) is the 'halve the flow' error that p3 explicitly warns against — doubling one layer does not double the total resistance — so the item tests the paragraph as well as the arithmetic. Full ablation (independent-ablation-1): above-chance without the pack (would have chosen "b", confidence 0.45) — Same bounded reasoning as q2: the answer must be between half and all of the original flow, and only the (180 W -> 100 W) pairing gives an insulation-dominant wall consistent with q3's key. Derived from cross-question constraints, not from the figure's numbers.

adjudicator.model: independent-ablation-1 (full ablation) + independent-blind-1 (blind re-answer)

gam-eng-tr-001-q5.rationale: Blind re-answer (independent-blind-1, confidence 0.95): Block p2 states that because the resistances are added, layer order does not change the total, so the steady flow is unchanged. Option d reaches the same verdict by a false reason (temperature difference alone does not fix the flow — resistance does too), so a careless marker could call d half-right, but the text's own justification is the one in c and d's reason is contradicted by f1. I still count exactly one defensible option because the stem asks 'according to the text' and demands the reason. Full ablation (independent-ablation-1): determinable without the pack (would have chosen "c", confidence 0.9) — Series thermal resistances add, and addition is commutative, so layer order cannot change the steady-state flow. Option d gives the right verdict for the wrong reason (it ignores resistance entirely), which is the standard near-miss distractor.

adjudicator.model: independent-ablation-1 (full ablation) + independent-blind-1 (blind re-answer)

gam-eng-tr-001-q6.rationale: Blind re-answer (independent-blind-1, confidence 0.94): Block p3 states the total is a sum of positive terms and so always larger than any single layer's resistance, and that adding a layer can only reduce the flow — which refutes c. Option d is refuted by p1 (the same heat passes through every layer). The one wrinkle is that a is only strictly true because every layer has positive resistance, which the text asserts rather than proves; the stem's 'several layers' framing keeps it safe. Full ablation (independent-ablation-1): determinable without the pack (would have chosen "a", confidence 0.85) — In series the total is the sum of strictly positive resistances, so it exceeds any single layer; c is false because any added layer adds resistance, and d is false because the same heat flow passes through every layer in steady state. Pure physics.

gam-hum-sc-001-q1.rationale: Blind re-answer (independent-blind-1, confidence 0.96): Block p3 says proximity 'concerns the route by which the information reached the author'. Options a and c restate the attribution and interest checks and d restates the independence discussion in p5, so all three are the pack's own other concepts. The checks are named by this text, so the pack defines the term being tested. Full ablation (independent-ablation-1): determinable without the pack (would have chosen "b", confidence 0.8) — The framework's three names are recoverable from the sibling questions (attribution, proximity, interest). Proximity is by definition how close the author stood to the events, i.e. the route by which the information reached them; a is attribution, c is interest and d is textual filiation.

adjudicator.model: independent-ablation-1 (full ablation) + independent-blind-1 (blind re-answer)

gam-hum-sc-001-q2.rationale: Blind re-answer (independent-blind-1, confidence 0.95): Block p2 defines attribution as whether the document was written by the named person at the claimed time and place, and says physical evidence such as the writing material can settle it on its own — which is exactly the paper-dating fact in the stem. Option d is the only rival worth weighing: a mis-copied date would still mean the document is not what it presents itself as, so it fails attribution either way. Full ablation (independent-ablation-1): determinable without the pack (would have chosen "a", confidence 0.8) — Paper postdating the claimed date shows the document was not produced by the named signatory, which is precisely the authenticity/attribution question. Option d is the hedged escape and does not survive an 80-year material anachronism. Standard source criticism.

adjudicator.model: independent-ablation-1 (full ablation) + independent-blind-1 (blind re-answer)

gam-hum-sc-001-q3.rationale: Blind re-answer (independent-blind-1, confidence 0.9): The stem removes the interest check by stipulation ('gained nothing') and p3's ladder — witness, told by a participant, later compiler — places a monk working sixty years later from circulating stories at the far end, so proximity is at issue and fares badly. Option d inverts the concept (community closeness is not informational proximity) and c misapplies attribution. Mild looseness: the stem does not absolutely exclude that some circulating story came from a participant, so 'nor told by one' is a slightly stronger claim than the stem strictly licenses — not enough to make d or a defensible. Full ablation (independent-ablation-1): determinable without the pack (would have chosen "b", confidence 0.85) — The stem deliberately neutralises the interest check ('gained nothing') and the attribution check is not in question, leaving proximity, which sixty years of oral transmission fails. Option d inverts the meaning of proximity (community closeness is not closeness to the event).

adjudicator.model: independent-ablation-1 (full ablation) + independent-blind-1 (blind re-answer)

gam-hum-sc-001-q4.rationale: Blind re-answer (independent-blind-1, confidence 0.96): Block p6 supplies exactly this case: a forged charter is worthless for the transactions it records but direct evidence for the concerns of the period in which it was forged, and the historian's question here is about that very period. Option a contradicts p6's opening sentence. Worth noting that the item reuses the pack's own worked example almost unchanged, so it tests recognition more than transfer. Full ablation (independent-ablation-1): determinable without the pack (would have chosen "c", confidence 0.9) — The standard historiographical point: a forgery is authentic evidence for its own moment of production, and the stem has been constructed so that the forgery date coincides with the period under investigation. No source text required.

adjudicator.model: independent-ablation-1 (full ablation) + independent-blind-1 (blind re-answer)

gam-hum-sc-001-q5.rationale: Blind re-answer (independent-blind-1, confidence 0.95): Block p5 states that where several texts descend from one lost original their agreement establishes only that the copying was faithful, and that the number of copies makes no difference — option b is that sentence restated, and a is the fallacy it names. My reservation is not correctness but weight: the stem itself supplies the common-descent fact, and the inference from 'all three copy one lost source' to 'agreement shows only faithful copying' is available to ordinary reasoning, so the pack is close to decorative here; a candidate who never read p5 lands on b anyway. Option d is also unsupported in either direction (the text nowhere says close agreement suggests invention). Full ablation (independent-ablation-1): determinable without the pack (would have chosen "b", confidence 0.9) — Texts descending from a common exemplar are one witness, not three, so their agreement establishes only faithful copying and adds no independent attestation. Textbook stemmatics.

adjudicator.model: independent-ablation-1 (full ablation) + independent-blind-1 (blind re-answer)

gam-hum-sc-001-q6.rationale: Blind re-answer (independent-blind-1, confidence 0.94): Option c is p1 almost verbatim ('a document may pass one and fail another, and each has to be applied on its own'), a is refuted by p6, b by p1's 'rather than blurred into a single impression', and d by p4's 'unaffected by how near the author stood'. So the answer is right and unique — but the three distractors are all absolutist or self-evidently overreaching, and c is the generically sensible statement, so a test-wise candidate picks it without reading the pack. That plus the verbatim lift is why I marked the source non-load-bearing: the item measures option plausibility rather than comprehension. Full ablation (independent-ablation-1): determinable without the pack (would have chosen "c", confidence 0.85) — The three checks test different properties, so they are logically independent and applied separately; a is refuted by q4's forgery case in the same set, b collapses distinct dimensions into one score, and d asserts an entailment that plainly does not hold.
